Title: Diagnosis of test `testTwoCompleteOptions`
Details:
The test `testTwoCompleteOptions` tries to create two options in the same test using `OptionBuilder`.

The test starts by creating the first option `simple` using the builder methods such as `withLongOpt`, `hasArg`, `isRequired`, `hasArgs`, `withType(Float.class)`, and `withDescription`. Then, it calls `create('s')` to create the `Option`. The `OptionBuilder.create(char)` internally calls `create(String)`, that creates a new `Option` with all the currently stored properties such as `description`, `longopt`, `required`, `type`, etc. After creating the option, `OptionBuilder.reset()` is called to reset all static fields back to default.

Then, the test tries to create another option using the same `OptionBuilder` static instance, with different properties: only `withLongOpt("dimple option")`, `hasArg()`, and `withDescription`. It then calls `create('d')` to create this second option.

The problem is that after the first call to `create('s')`, the static fields in `OptionBuilder` have been reset. The second option is built only with some properties set, but some properties such as `type` have not been explicitly set again. Therefore, the value of `type` for the second option is the default (which seems to be `String.class`).

This leads to failing the test assertion `assertEquals( String.class, simple.getType() );` for the second `simple` option (the "dimple option"), because the first option set the type to `Float.class` but that state was reset and the second option has to explicitly define its own type if expected to be anything other than the default.

In summary, the issue occurs because `OptionBuilder` uses static fields and resets them with each option created, causing state leakage between option creations, and the second option does not set all fields explicitly.

The failing test probably assumes the type of the second option will be the default type `String.class`, but because the first option set it to `Float.class` and was reset, the second option did not override `type`, so it defaults correctly but the test is expecting something else.

The key methods involved in this malfunction are:
- `OptionBuilder.create(String)` (lines 351-376): creates the `Option` using the static state from `OptionBuilder` then resets the builder.
- `OptionBuilder.reset()` (lines 79-89): resets all static fields after option creation.
- Builder setter methods such as `withLongOpt`, `hasArg`, `isRequired`, `hasArgs`, `withType` that set the static fields.

Since the builder uses static state, state from one option interferes with other options unless all fields are explicitly set each time.

---
